title: Weight of a constant twist
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-weil-punctual-weights]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $q=p^a>1$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal F=(M,\theta)$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w\in\mathbf R$.

For $b\in\Qlb^\times$, put $\mathcal F_b=(M,b\theta)$, with inverse structure map $b^{-1}\theta^{-1}$; scalar morphisms are computed over a common finite coefficient extension [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Let $J_X$ be the coefficient equivalence on Weil pairs of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. In the PBC model [def-wf-weil-category], use the explicit constant Weil line $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}=J_X(E_X,b\theta_E)$ of [lem-wf-constant-twist-coefficient-comparison], where $(E_X,\theta_E)$ is [def-weil-constant-weil-structure] at any finite field $E$ containing $b$. Its tensor with $J_X(\mathcal F)$ is the completed derived tensor of [def-wf-tensor-product], and its punctual weights mean the weights after transport back to [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

If $c\in\mathbf R$ satisfies $2\log_q|\iota(b)|=c$, then both $\mathcal F_b$ and the transported tensor $J_X(\mathcal F)\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}$ are punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w+c$. On the geometrically connected domain where the representation prescription of [def-wf-constant-weil-twist] defines $\mathcal B_b$, the comparison identifies $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}$ with that specified line. In particular the blueprint tensor $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w+c$ there. On arbitrary separated finite-type $X_0$ the explicit line $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}$ supplies the constant-line tensor assertion without a geometric-connectedness or lisse hypothesis.

proof.text: The scalar twist in the statement is an object of precisely the category in which purity is defined. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], compute $b$, $\theta$ and $\theta^{-1}$ over a common finite coefficient extension. The morphism groups and scalar-extension formula in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] make scalar multiplication compatible with a further extension, so $b\theta$ is a well-defined morphism $Lg_X^*M\to M$ in that common-stage category. Bilinearity of composition gives $(b\theta)(b^{-1}\theta^{-1})=\operatorname{id}_M$ and $(b^{-1}\theta^{-1})(b\theta)=\operatorname{id}_{Lg_X^*M}$. Thus [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], items 1 and 3, makes $(M,b\theta)$ a Weil sheaf: its underlying object is still $M$ in the constructible heart. This construction does not require a Weil-group representation or any tensor-product comparison.

source.place: First sentence, constant twist, with its intrinsic scalar-rescaling meaning made explicit; statement correction R1/R2

proof.text: Fix a closed point $y$ of degree $m\geq1$. In [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], the local operator is obtained by the point transport, the pullback-composition comparison, and the pullback of $\theta^{[m]}$. Pullbacks are coefficient-linear by the rational-stage formulas of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The recurrence for the iterates in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] therefore gives $(b\theta)^{[m]}=b^m\theta^{[m]}$: it holds for $m=1$, and the next composite multiplies $b^m$ by the additional $b$. The point transport and composition comparison depend only on the unchanged underlying object. The point fiber is coefficient-linear by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Consequently the local Frobenius on the twist, for the pair constructed in Step 1, is $b^m F_y$. This uses the local definition itself, without identifying a general constructible sheaf with a global fundamental-group representation.

source.place: First sentence: Frobenius at a point of degree m is multiplied by b^m

proof.text: Put $V=\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ and $t=b^m\ne0$. If $v\ne0$ and $(tF_y)v=\beta v$, then $F_yv=(\beta/t)v$; conversely $F_yv=\alpha v$ implies $(tF_y)v=(t\alpha)v$. Thus every eigenvalue of the twisted local operator is $b^m\alpha$ for an eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_y$. The calculation does not assume diagonalizability. When $V=0$ there are no eigenvalues and the assertion is vacuous.

source.place: First sentence: every eigenvalue alpha becomes b^m alpha

proof.text:
Write $r=|\iota(b)|>0$. Since $q>1$, the hypothesis $2\log_q r=c$ says $\log r=(c/2)\log q$, hence $r=q^{c/2}$. At a closed point of degree $m$, $q_y=\#\kappa(y)=q^m$. Punctual purity of $\mathcal F$, as defined in [def-weil-punctual-weights], gives $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_y^{w/2}$. For the eigenvalue from Step 3, multiplicativity of $\iota$ and the complex norm give
$$|\iota(b^m\alpha)|=r^m q_y^{w/2}=q^{mc/2}q^{mw/2}=q_y^{(w+c)/2}.$$
Here the identities for real powers follow by writing each as $\exp(s\log q)$, with positive base $q$. Every closed point and every eigenvalue were arbitrary, so [def-weil-punctual-weights] gives the asserted purity of weight $w+c$.

source.place: Displayed norm identity and final sentence

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-constant-twist-coefficient-comparison] to $\mathcal F$ and $b$. It identifies the PBC tensor $J_X(\mathcal F)\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}$, transported to the common-stage model, with $\mathcal F_b$ as a constructible Weil sheaf, and gives intertwining isomorphisms of their local Frobenius spaces. If $A T=T' A$ and $A$ is invertible, a nonzero eigenvector $v$ of $T$ maps to the nonzero eigenvector $Av$ of $T'$ with the same eigenvalue; applying $A^{-1}$ gives the converse. Thus the two local operators have the same eigenvalues. Step 4 and [def-weil-punctual-weights] give purity of the transported tensor of weight $w+c$. On the geometrically connected domain of [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], the same comparison identifies the explicit line with the specified $\mathcal B_b$, so this is purity of the actual blueprint tensor $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$. For other schemes the explicit constant line in the comparison gives the asserted tensor construction directly.

blueprint_update.statement:
If $\mathcal F$ is a Weil sheaf, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w$, and $2\log_q|\iota(b)|=c$, then
$\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w+c$.

proof.text:
At a closed point $y$ of degree $m$, the twist
[def-wf-constant-weil-twist] multiplies every eigenvalue of
$F_y$ by $b^m$, so every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of
$\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ becomes $b^m\alpha$, and

$$
|\iota(b^m\alpha)|=|\iota(b)|^m\,q_y^{w/2}=q^{mc/2}q^{mw/2}
=q_y^{(w+c)/2},
$$

which is the punctual purity of weight $w+c$ of
[def-weil-punctual-weights].
